/hotels/australia/united-places-botanic-.note: Brutalist lines, clean and minimal, softened by Italian-made pieces from Moroso and Patricia Urquiola. Suites are private and spacious, built for lingering, each with a large sunken bathtub. Ask for a Garden Suite: it looks north across the Royal Botanic Gardens, trees rustling beyond a deep terrace balcony. Then open the minibar for Sullivan's Cove Double Cask whisky or Mount Mary's Pinot Noir. Booked through Aspen, daily breakfast comes with the stay, and an upgrade on arrival may follow, subject to availability. The city sits 15 minutes away.

/hotels/bermuda/the-loren-at-pink-beach-.note: Pink sand, turquoise Atlantic, and floor-to-ceiling glass to take it all in. The Loren sits on Bermuda's south shore with a boutique, artistic streak and only 48 rooms, so it reads as a hideaway rather than a sprawl. Days drift between the oceanfront pool, sea-inspired treatments in the Sisley Spa and seasonal plates at The Pink Beach Club. Want your own water? Ask for the One Bed Villa, with its ocean-facing balcony and private heated pool. Booked through Aspen, there is a daily breakfast credit and welcome cocktails for two.

/hotels/canada/rental-escapes-montreal.note: Less a hotel than a key to a very good villa. A chateau among Bordeaux vineyards. A glass-walled Thai villa, beach just outside. A restored mansion in Cartagena. A treehouse-style suite in the Sabi Sand. Many arrive fully staffed, so relaxing is the only job left, and the concierge can conjure a personal chef, a car and driver, even a yacht charter. Booked through Aspen, you get an Experiences Credit to spend during your stay. Plan it with the concierge, as it can't be put toward the villa rate.

/hotels/canada/wedgewood-hotel-and-spa-v.note: Downtown Vancouver, set among Robson Square's gardens and waterfalls, yet the place feels intimate. Family owned and run. Look for the hidden corners: the Library Room for private dinners, the Chelsea Garden Patio. Bacchus Restaurant & Lounge serves modern European cooking, Michelin-recommended. Penthouse Suites come with antiques, original paintings and colours all their own. Want a deep soaker tub in Roman marble? Ask for a Deluxe Executive Guestroom. Booked through Aspen, full breakfast is daily for up to two per bedroom, with an upgrade on arrival when available.

/hotels/china/qiushui-villa-hangzhou.note: A restored villa on West Lake, built to slow you down. Steps cross a shimmering pool to reach the door; stone statues and bright flowers line the courtyard. Inside, antiques chosen by hand, a butler who takes requests in stride, French cooking, and an infinity pool for staring at the famous view. Lofts and suites carry the names of historical figures. Four travelling together should ask for the Mei Gui Qing, the only two-bedroom loft. Booked through Aspen, breakfast comes daily and private airport transfers run both ways.

/hotels/china/the-silk-lakehouse-shangri.note: A silk merchant's home, reimagined on the edge of West Lake. Inside: landscape murals, silk textiles, motifs borrowed from fauna. Rooms look out over the water toward Baoshi Mountain, or onto a bamboo garden. Ask for the Premier Room, Lakeview; its floor-to-ceiling view is the lake itself. Evenings belong to the Sky Garden lounge on the roof and its wide panorama. Chef Alan Yu's bistro fare waits in The Living Room. Booked through Aspen, daily buffet breakfast is included, plus a food and beverage credit worth spending on cocktails. A private ambassador handles the rest.

/hotels/france/cour-des-loges-lyon.note: A Renaissance jewel in Vieux Lyon, wrapped in a maze of courtyards, corridors and staircases from the days of the traboules and silk workers. Losing your way comes easily. Mornings open with a buffet breakfast in a lush courtyard. Later, bistro dishes at Le Comptoir. By evening, candlelight and Lyon classics given a gastronomic turn at Les Loges, then a retro bar pouring Cognac, Armagnac and single malts. Ask for a Collection Premium Room overlooking the cobblestone streets. Booked through Aspen, daily full breakfast for up to two is included, along with a food and beverage credit.

/hotels/france/le-royal-monceau-raffles-.note: A Palace that treats art as a house guest. Expect a private gallery, a screening room and an Art Concierge to steer you through works on the property and across Paris. Several rooms carry Philippe Starck design; the Gallery Suite comes dressed in sculptures and photos. Dinner might be Il Carpaccio, Michelin-starred and Italian, or Matsuhisa Paris. Then the long pool at the spa. The tip: book a Signature Suite or higher through Aspen and private airport transfers come both ways, alongside breakfast each day for two guests.

/hotels/france/les-roches-rouges-saint-r.note: Red rock, blue water, pine on the breeze. Les Roches Rouges sits beneath the Estérel Massif, a retro-modern hotel designed as a terrace above the Mediterranean. Days arrange themselves: a swim in the saltwater pool, a spell on the private beach, focaccia at La Chicoula, something more Provençal at Estelo. Want the sea on waking? Ask for a Deluxe room. Every one faces the water. Booked through Aspen, a daily breakfast buffet covers up to two guests per room, and an upgrade on arrival is possible, subject to availability.

/hotels/germany/hotel-de-rome-berlin-ber.note: A bank once lived here, and it left its vault behind. Today that vault holds De Rome Spa, with a gym and a long menu of beauty treatments. At the door, the mood shifts: magenta urns, a neon birdcage, a stone entrance with real presence. Evenings belong to the Rooftop Terrace, cocktail in hand, skyline coming alight. Ask for a Premier Room, which looks out over Bebel Square. Booked through Aspen, a buffet breakfast each morning for two comes included, plus a credit for food, drink or the spa. Spend it in the vault.

/hotels/greece/bill-and-coo-hotels-mykon.note: Megali Ammos, on the edge of Mykonos. Every room here is a suite, and every suite faces the sunset; some keep a pool or plunge pool all to themselves, which is worth asking for. Mornings start with breakfast made to order, then the infinity pool. Evenings belong to the Sunset Lounge: a signature cocktail, Greek small bites from chef Ntinos Fotinakis, the sun sliding into the sea. Dinner follows at the Gastronomy Project. Book through Aspen and an upgrade on arrival may be waiting, subject to availability. The Valmont Spa handles the rest.

/hotels/greece/mykonos-grand-hotel-and-r.note: Whitewashed cubes, cobbled paths, and Delos sitting opposite. The mood is Zen, the selling points seclusion and wellness, and rooms are scattered widely so neighbours stay a rumour. Spa treatments come poolside or in a seaside cabana. Hora is a stroll away. Dinner is open-air, Greek, and staged against the sunset. For privacy, ask for the Signature Suite, set at the property's edge with its own pool and Aegean views. Booked through Aspen, daily full breakfast is included, and an upgrade on arrival may come your way, subject to availability.

/hotels/indonesia/como-uma-bali.note: The supplier's file is brief, almost monastic. A COMO property. In Ubud, on Bali, in Indonesia. Filed under city hotel, which is all the paperwork says about the setting, and this note won't embroider it. What you get is a name, a brand, and an address left to do the rest of the talking. The practical move: this hotel sits within the Virtuoso advisor programme, so ask your Aspen Travel Advisors contact what that listing could mean for your stay before you commit. Then let the place speak.

/hotels/indonesia/raffles-bali-bali.note: Tropical gardens tumble down a hillside to a secluded beach, known to guests and a few local fishermen and nobody else. Just 32 villas share the slope. A wellness butler shapes every visit. Days drift between spa, meditation terrace and the beachfront infinity pool, a Bali Sling within reach. Dinner might be in the Secret Cave. If sunsets matter, ask for a Panoramic Pool Villa. Booked through Aspen, private airport transfers are complimentary both ways, and an upgrade on arrival is possible, subject to availability.

/hotels/ireland/sheen-falls-lodge-county.note: Water is the theme here. The Sheen River runs past the deluxe rooms, waterfalls tumble through the grounds, and Kenmare Bay sits at the door. Woodland walks, salmon fishing, falconry, kayaking, golf with a free shuttle to the course. Or the spa and an indoor pool, if you'd rather not. The Falls Restaurant hangs over the waterfall and every table gets the view, so plan at least one evening there. Through Aspen, a bottle of house wine waits in the room, and a vintage Buick takes you round Kenmare.

/hotels/israel/the-ritz-carlton-herzliya.note: The Mediterranean out front, the Herzliya Marina below, and a private balcony on every room to take in the sea. The style is sophisticated. A kosher restaurant handles the serious dining, and the lobby bar handles the signature cocktails. Higher up, a rooftop pool on the 12th floor keeps its own bar. The spa runs to a sauna and a Turkish hammam. Tip: ask about the Studio Suite, with its kitchenette and waterfront deck balcony. Booked through Aspen, buffet breakfast comes daily, and an upgrade on arrival is possible, subject to availability.

/hotels/italy/casa-cipriani-milano-milan.note: Gentlemen's club mood, Milanese address, just 15 rooms and suites. Ask for the Signature Suite or a Premier Corner Room: oak floors, walnut boiserie and a Venini chandelier overhead. A butler is on hand. In the spa, Finnish saunas, a Hammam and a steam bath clad in green onyx. Booked through Aspen, full breakfast comes daily for up to two, plus a food and beverage credit. Spend some on a Bellini, naturally. Then pack a picnic and wander over to Giardini Indro Montanelli, a rare patch of green in Milan.

/hotels/italy/cascioni-eco-retreat-sardi.note: Granite, olive trees, myrtle on the air. The retreat keeps things earthy: rooms with Sardinian names, dressed in tones that answer the land around them. A stream runs into the protected Saloni Lagoon, and you can cool off in it. Ask for a Deluxe Pool Suite for your own portico, garden and pool. Booked through Aspen, a complimentary massage for two per bedroom comes once during your stay, so pencil it in early. The concierge can line up kayaking, RIB boating or a hand in the olive harvest.

/hotels/italy/palazzo-fiuggi-fiuggi.note: Wellness here is taken seriously. It starts with an evaluation and diagnostics, then a tailored pathway of medical and spa therapies, and a follow-up plan to hold the results over the long term. The healing springs are part of the programme. A trainer waits in the Movement Lab, with virtual-reality machines and a Pilates room. Meals are organic and biodynamic, a personal menu shaped by Heinz Beck. Worth knowing: book a Suite or higher through Aspen and the spa credit grows. The Imperial Suite's terrace overlooks the old town.

/hotels/italy/villa-d-este-cernobbio-lak.note: Two historic mansions, a landscaped park and a lake that does most of the talking. Every room at Villa d'Este is decorated in its own way, so expect character rather than uniformity. Dine on gourmet Italian at Veranda, or loosen the collar at Grill. Then there is the pool, heated and floating on Lake Como itself. Book through Aspen and you may be upgraded on arrival, availability permitting. The tip: take a suite, which brings Premium Champagne, fruit, flowers and friandises to greet you.

/hotels/jamaica/the-cliff-hotel-negril.note: Open-air lobby, bare feet, the Caribbean Sea below. The Cliff Hotel sits on a private bluff in Negril's secluded West End, a retreat of suites and villas with a cosmopolitan streak and a Jamaican accent. Dinner might be jerked chicken penne pasta. The KiYara Spa leans on indigenous botanicals and herbs, in rooms that face the ocean. Ask for a One Bedroom Suite with Pool, and the Nespresso machine comes loaded with Blue Mountain coffee. Booked through Aspen, daily full breakfast is included, plus an upgrade on arrival when available.

/hotels/malta/intercontinental-malta-st-.note: St Julian's, beachside, with Valletta a short hop away. Days here split between a lagoon-style pool and a private sandy beach, with an award-winning spa and Cynergi, the island's largest gym, for the virtuous. Six restaurants, six bars, some seasonal: Neapolitan pizza at Lubelli, fine dining at SKYBEACH. The tip: ask for a Highline suite. Higher floors, the Club InterContinental lounge, the SKYBEACH infinity pool, and, booked through Aspen, private airport transfers both ways. Early check-in at 11:00AM comes confirmed when you book, so the day starts early.

/hotels/mexico/la-casa-de-la-playa-playa.note: Adults only, and every suite keeps its own private pool. A butler handles the rest. The design leans Mexican and contemporary, all craft and calm, with Muluk Spa for when lying still feels like too much effort. Ask for an Ocean Front Suite: the Caribbean Sea fills the view from bed, pool or terrace. The Wellness suites offer spa service in the room, if leaving it seems excessive. Book through Aspen and breakfast arrives daily, with an upgrade on arrival when availability allows. Seclusion, mostly. That is the point.

/hotels/monaco/hotel-hermitage-monte-car.note: Casino Square is a short stroll away, the Mediterranean spreads below, and the Belle Epoque does the rest. Look up in the Winter Garden for the Eiffel cupola. Gustave, the new bar, waits beneath the dome. Dinner runs from Pavyllon to Japanese fine dining at l'Abysse, and champagne lives in the garden, courtesy of Perrier-Jouët. Booked through Aspen, there's daily buffet breakfast for up to two and a food and beverage credit. Spend it on a drink at Gustave; the minibar doesn't count. Suite seekers should ask about the Riviera: sun-filled, panoramic sea views.

/hotels/montenegro/mamula-island-by-bany.note: A restored fortress, ringed by water. Mamula Island sits in Boka Bay, with wild scenery and views that reach well out over the Adriatic. Inside, original features meet custom-crafted furniture and local art. There is a spa, a beach, several pools, and kayaks or water bikes for the shoreline. Ask for a Panoramic Room, high in the fort's tower on its top floor. Book through Aspen and a massage is included once during your stay, plus either water or e-bike time or a trip to the Blue Cave.

/hotels/morocco/kasbah-tamadot-asni.note: Snow-capped Atlas peaks to the south. To the north, a steep river valley of limestone and forest. Across the river sits a Berber village built into the mountainside, and the staff are local, drawn from the surrounding villages. Days go to walking the mountains, or riding a mule, then a hammam, the infinity-edge pool, a cooking lesson. Ask for a Berber tent: private hot tub, real seclusion, a sky made for stargazing. Booked through Aspen, there is hotel credit for spa, gift shop or dining, and an upgrade on arrival when available.

/hotels/new-zealand/rosewood-cape-kidnap.note: Farmland rolls out to cliffs, and the cliffs fall straight into the sea. Out here a sheep and cattle station still at work shares the land with a spa, a sanctuary for precious flora and fauna, and a golf course where every hole looks at the ocean. Each suite has its own balcony and a sitting area. Families: ask for a Hilltop Family Suite, up on the hilltop above the lodge. And don't skip the guests-only Kiwi Discovery Walk. Booked through Aspen, breakfast comes daily, and an upgrade on arrival is possible, subject to availability.

/hotels/new-zealand/sofitel-auckland-via.note: Harbour on one side, a French accent on the other. Sofitel Auckland does chic without the fuss. Rooms bring floor-to-ceiling glass, big bathrooms with rain showers and deep tubs, and the bed Sofitel calls MyBed. La Marée puts a French zest on fresh local produce. Arriving jet-lagged? Book the Traveller's Revival Massage or the De-Stress Eye Treatment at Sofitel Spa. Reserve through Aspen and full breakfast for up to two guests is served daily in the restaurant, with an upgrade on arrival when availability allows.

/hotels/portugal/olissippo-lapa-palace-l.note: A hilltop palace above the River Tagus, wrapped in quiet gardens where fountains and streams do the talking. Inside: carved wood, marble stucco, azulejos in rich patterns. Every room has a terrace over garden or river, so choose your view wisely. Want the water? Ask for a Palace Deluxe Room or a River View Room. Book through Aspen and you arrive to port wine and chocolate chip cookies, with an upgrade if one is free. Evenings belong to the Rio Tejo Bar, drink in hand, river below.

/hotels/saint-barthelemy/eden-rock-st-ba.note: A hotel built on a rock, quite literally. It sits on a promontory at Baie de Saint Jean, turquoise sea below, coral reefs offshore, soft white sand at the back door. The style is hip. Villa Nina sits right on the beach, with a dedicated chef and butler. For height and theatre, ask about the Howard Hughes suite: a loft crowning the main house, terraces all round and a full-circle view. Booked through Aspen, expect an upgrade on arrival when available, plus a beach bag and flip flops per room.

/hotels/south-africa/mateya-safari-lodge.note: Five suites. Ten guests, at most. Out on the plains of the Madikwe Game Reserve, the lodge was built from materials gathered in the reserve itself, and the land runs down toward the Marico River. Your suite comes with a fireplace, a terrace and a private pool. The rangers double as serious wildlife photographers, so reserve a private safari vehicle and let them steer your lens. Booked through Aspen, there's a complimentary massage for two per room, once in your stay. Malaria-free, too. Casual in style, and quietly secluded.

/hotels/spain/hotel-arts-barcelona-barce.note: Tallest hotel on the coast, and it knows it. Panoramic views run from city to beach, the rooms are light-filled, and the eating is serious: four restaurants, a cocktail bar, and Enoteca Paco Pérez with its two Michelin stars. The family pool looks over the gardens, calm by day and lively after dark. Ask for a room facing the city and the Sagrada Familia. Booked through Aspen, buffet breakfast is included daily for up to two guests, and an upgrade on arrival is possible, subject to availability. Some common areas are partly closed for renovation.

/hotels/thailand/aman-nai-lert-bangkok-b.note: A tower of calm rising from Nai Lert Park, right in the centre of Bangkok. Just 52 suites. Seven signature dining venues, and a spa spread over two floors for undoing the day. The style is Zen, the mood tranquil. Ask for a Premier Corner Suite: park canopy to the south, sunsets to the west. Booked through Aspen, breakfast is daily and an upgrade on arrival may come your way, subject to availability. Stay two nights or more and a limousine handles the airport run both ways.

/hotels/turkiye/tafoni-houses-cave-hotel.note: Eighteen cave suites, every one of them a nest. The rooms carry bird names, Hoopoe, Swallow, Kingfisher, and come dressed in vintage furniture, original art and antiques. Outside, terraces look over carved valleys and rock formations, while a lived-in town goes about its business around you. Dinner is at the Nest, a cave restaurant pouring Cappadocian wines. Booked through Aspen, breakfast arrives daily and one lunch or dinner for two is on the house. The tip: stay four nights or more and a second complimentary meal joins the first.

/hotels/united-arab-emirates/anantara-mi.note: A private peninsula of golden sand, wrapped in mangroves, with lagoon giving way to open ocean. Ask for an Over Water Pool Villa, the first of its kind in the emirate, and take your morning espresso on the terrace. Days fill easily. Yoga, a Thai spa ritual, flyboards and e-foils, sandboarding, golf, the world's longest zipline. The kitchens roam from Asia to the Mediterranean, and sunset brings cocktails and shisha. Booked through Aspen, a daily buffet breakfast is included, plus resort credit to spend during your stay.

/hotels/united-kingdom/chewton-glen-new-.note: Ancient forest on one side, the sea on the other. Chewton Glen started life as a country house and grew into a small resort: a spa, a cookery school, a kitchen garden that stocks the dining room, and Treehouse Suites for anyone who wants the woods closer. In the room, expect a fireplace, a whirlpool tub, slippers and turndown. Booked through Aspen, full breakfast comes daily, along with a hotel credit. Spend it at the spa. Sailing from Southampton? The docks are 35 minutes away, so arrive the night before.

/hotels/united-states/1-hotel-brooklyn-b.note: A waterfront hotel at Pier 1 in Brooklyn Bridge Park, looking straight across the East River at the Manhattan skyline. Inside: reclaimed materials, native greenery, the hand of local artists, and windows that run floor to ceiling. Industrial chic with a soft side. Dinner is farm-to-table at The Osprey; evenings belong to the plunge pool and bar up on the roof. For the bridge itself, ask for a Bridge King, whose large sliding window opens onto it. Booked through Aspen, you get an upgrade on arrival, subject to availability, plus a daily breakfast credit.

/hotels/united-states/austin-proper-hote.note: Downtown Austin, the Second Street District, and interiors that refuse to be beige. Designer Kelly Wearstler sets the tone, and the mood leans whimsical. Wellness runs to sports massages, sound bath rituals and a recovery room. Evenings rise to the rooftop pool for small-batch tequila at sunset, or settle into Kappo Kappo, a French Japanese omakase served across a chef's counter. Want a little open air of your own? Ask for the Proper Balcony Suite. Booked through Aspen, you get a daily breakfast credit, plus a room upgrade at check-in when available.

/hotels/united-states/fairmont-grand-del.note: A coastal canyon, a private golf course by Tom Fazio, and a spa that leans on nature. Trail rides wind into Los Penasquitos Canyon, out to its bluffs; hiking paths start right beside the resort. Dinner can mean Addison, the city's first Michelin-Three Star table. Four pools, but the one to find is the Relaxation Pool: adults only, next to the spa, with speakers underwater for a meditative swim. Book through Aspen and a daily breakfast credit is yours, plus an upgrade on arrival when one is free.

/hotels/united-states/four-seasons-hotel.note: Downtown Austin, but with a lakeside resort attitude. The hotel sits on the shore of Lady Bird Lake, wrapped in gardens, with the Hike & Bike Trail right next door for anyone who brought trainers. Others will prefer the saltwater pool, the spa, or a hammock beneath a heritage oak. Rooms look out over either the lake or the city. Ask for a Lake View Suite if water is the point. Booked through Aspen, breakfast comes daily for up to two per bedroom. And yes, there is a margarita button on the room phone.

/hotels/united-states/grand-hyatt-kauai-.note: White sand underfoot, lush gardens and pools with a sense of humour. A river pool meanders. A waterslide waits. Adults seeking quiet have their own pool, kayaks drift in the lagoons, and Anara Spa handles whatever tension survives. Open courtyards keep the mood casual. A tip: standard rooms may look onto lawns, gardens or mountains, and some catch the guest parking, so ask for a suite with a garden or ocean outlook. Booked through Aspen, a daily buffet breakfast for two per bedroom is included, plus an upgrade on arrival when available.

/hotels/united-states/limelight-boulder-.note: A new hotel on the campus of the University of Colorado, in University Hill, with the Flatirons in view from every floor. The best seat is the second-story pool deck: heated, with a hot tub and an outdoor fireplace. Ajax Tavern does inventive, locally sourced plates with an après buzz. All-electric, LEED Gold, with Audi e-tron courtesy cars and a free shuttle downtown. Ask for an Aspen One-Bedroom Suite, up on the higher floors, for the views. Booked through Aspen, there is a $100 property credit and a possible upgrade on arrival.

/hotels/united-states/park-hyatt-washing.note: Corner of 24th and M, where Georgetown meets the city centre. Inside, the mood is Zen: handcrafted furniture, museum-quality art, bathrooms built around deep soaking tubs. The suite list runs long, right up to penthouse level. Blue Duck Tavern brings the Michelin stars. Booked through Aspen, you get a daily breakfast credit in the restaurant and an upgrade on arrival, when available. Before heading for the Smithsonian museums a few blocks away, take the Mezzanine tour: an exclusive look at works from The Phillips Collection.

/hotels/united-states/salamander-middleb.note: Horse and wine country, and the estate leans into both. Rolling acres, an equestrian center, country trails best seen from the saddle. Off the horse: hands-on cooking classes, a zip line, the spa, a locally sourced dinner at Harrimans. Wineries wait within an hour's drive. Ask for a Terrace King and claim a large, semi private stone terrace with seating outside. Booked through Aspen, there's a daily breakfast credit, plus an upgrade on arrival when available. And try the human/horse synergy classes. Two programs. Pick one.

/hotels/united-states/the-huntington-hot.note: High on Nob Hill, across from Huntington Park, a grand old city hotel has woken up. Georgian bones, polished again. Textured furnishings, hand-finished touches, a residential hush that the busy city outside never quite manages. Downstairs, the reworked lobby bar draws a crowd; order the Nob Hill Old Fashioned and watch. Upstairs, ask for a corner suite, where the windows take in Grace Cathedral and the park. Book through Aspen and full breakfast comes daily, with an upgrade on arrival when one is free. Tranquil. Unfussy. Very San Francisco.

/hotels/united-states/the-maybourne-beve.note: Beverly Hills, done with a mid-century accent. Armchairs and ottomans nod to old L.A. design, marble bathrooms gleam, and museum-worthy art lines the walls. Up top, a cabana-lined rooftop pool looks out to the Hollywood sign and the Pacific. Below, the biggest spa in the neighbourhood. Plan your afternoon around Dante Beverly Hills, the rooftop restaurant: its $10 Martini Hour runs 3pm to 5pm daily. Booked through Aspen, you get a $95 breakfast credit each day per bedroom, and an upgrade on arrival when one is available.

/hotels/united-states/the-preserve-sport.note: Think of it as summer camp for grown-ups. Fly-fishing, clay-shooting, horses and an 18-hole golf course fill the days across 3,500 protected acres. Evenings lean toward European-inspired plates at Double Barrel Kitchen, or bourbon matched with dinner inside the Maker's Mark Hobbit House. Sleep in a cabin, tiny home, townhome or the main lodge. Woodland suites come with a patio, so ask for one. Booked through Aspen, daily full breakfast is included, and an upgrade on arrival is offered, subject to availability. Ask, too, about the scotch and cigar tasting pop-up.

/hotels/united-states/the-times-square-e.note: Times Square hums below. Up here, the skyline does the talking. Rooms come with down comforters, custom imported linens and bathrooms in natural stone with enclosed rainforest showers; some add a soaking tub. Dinner is in the hands of Michelin-starred chef John Fraser, and an open-air wellness deck waits for working off the evidence. Theaters and galleries sit within walking distance. Travelling as a family? Ask for the two-bedroom Penthouse Suite, with its terrace over Times Square. Booked through Aspen, you get a daily breakfast credit and an upgrade on arrival when one's available.

/hotels/uruguay/sofitel-montevideo-casin.note: Carrasco, steps from the beach, and a hotel that still wears its early-20th-century glamour. French flair throughout. Haute French cooking at the 1921 Restaurant, high tea with beach views in the Tea Gallery, a cocktail at Thays Lounge Bar, then the casino. The So SPA has sauna, Jacuzzi and an indoor/outdoor pool. The tip: ask for a Luxury Room. It is the same size as the Superior, but you get Río de la Plata views, a hand-painted ceiling and a marble bathtub. Booked through Aspen, buffet breakfast comes daily.

/hotels/vietnam/four-seasons-resort-the-.note: Thousands of palms, a private ribbon of Ha My Beach, and villas set to catch the sea by phong thuy. Lounges sit both indoors and out, and showers come with their own gardens. Ask for a pool villa: the swimming pool is yours alone. Infinity pools descend in three tiers. There is a cooking academy, a herb and vegetable farm, and a spa that those in the know call a must. Booked through Aspen, you get a resort credit and an upgrade on arrival when one is free. Hoi An is close by.

/journeys/cruise/aqua-expeditions-ambon-.note: Aboard Aqua Blu, from Ambon to Sorong, the voyage finds its character early. The first dinner is curated by chef Benjamin Cross while Ambon's northern coast slips astern. Then the Banda Islands, reached at sunrise, kora-kora war canoes waiting at the harbor, and Fort Nassau, the Dutch fort on Banda Neira, once the most fought-over island in the world. That afternoon, snorkeling or diving. Further on, Misool Island and Mayalibit Bay. The tip: on your first morning aboard, be on deck early, before the Banda Islands appear at sunrise.

/journeys/cruise/aqua-expeditions-galapa.note: Aqua Mare is a superyacht with as many crew as guests, which tells you most of what you need to know about the service. This is the western route. Punta Moreno and Urvina Bay one day, Fernandina/Isabela the next, then a finish around Black Turtle Cove and North Seymour. It starts gently, with lunch outdoors at a giant tortoise reserve before you ever board. Tip: keep the waterproof welcome bag within reach. Wet landings are part of the deal, and the bag is made for exactly that.

/journeys/cruise/atlas-ocean-voyages-ant.note: 16 days aboard World Traveller, and the Falklands come first. Carcass Island and Saunders Island share a single day, then Port Stanley, then open water again. The real prize lies further south: several days given over to the Antarctic Peninsula, with the Drake Passage as the long road home. Sea days pad the route generously. Bring a good book and a patient stomach. One practical point: the voyage leaves from Buenos Aires and finishes in Ushuaia, so book your flights as an open jaw, not a simple round trip.

/journeys/cruise/atlas-ocean-voyages-fir.note: Iceland, taken slowly and from the water. World Voyager, the Atlas Ocean Voyages ship, sets out from Reykjavík and works the Icelandic coast one harbour at a time, Akureyri and Grimsey among them, deep in Arctic territory. Then the mood shifts south. A day at sea, Kirkwall, Aberdeen, another stretch of open water, and finally Dover. Practical point: you board in one country and step off in another, so book flights to match. Fly into Reykjavík, out of the United Kingdom, and leave some slack before the first day.

/journeys/cruise/atlas-ocean-voyages-net.note: Dover first, then the ship heads out. World Navigator, operated by Atlas Ocean Voyages, gives Amsterdam two days and Copenhagen the same. That is the voyage's quiet luxury: time to linger ashore rather than sprint back to the gangway. In between comes a canal transit through Germany, plus smaller calls at Harlingen and Wismar, before Skagen and a finish in Fredrikstad, Norway. The tip: treat the canal day as a day aboard, and save your energy for the long stays in Amsterdam and Copenhagen.

/journeys/cruise/aurora-expeditions-pata.note: Fjords first, then the big names. The Sylvia Earle threads Chilean channels such as the Moraleda and Kirke Narrows, and some days are simply left to the captain's choice, which is how an expedition ought to run. Puerto Natales opens the way to Torres del Paine National Park. Later, the Strait of Magellan, the Beagle Canal and Cape Horn crowd into a single day before Ushuaia. A tip: on arrival in Puerto Varas, find the hospitality desk in the hotel lobby that afternoon, collect your luggage tags, and mark your cabin number clearly.

/journeys/cruise/hx-expeditions-antarcti.note: Steak first, ice later. Buenos Aires comes first, an overnight in the city of the porteños, where parrillas serve Argentine steak and the tango claims its hometown. Then a flight to Ushuaia, and the voyage proper, aboard MS Roald Amundsen or MS Fridtjof Nansen. The Drake Passage, crossed going out and coming back. Between the crossings, the long stretch everyone came for: day after day cruising Antarctica. Practical point: arrive in Buenos Aires a few days early. The city rewards the extra time.

/journeys/cruise/national-geographic-lin.note: Sea Cloud II carries a great deal of sail, and on this Caribbean week she makes a show of it. You board late in the afternoon, champagne in hand, and slip out into a warm evening. Then the real theatre. After breakfast on Day 2 the crew climb the rigging and set sail by hand, while the captain narrates each manoeuvre and adds a little sea lore. Do not linger over coffee; be on deck for it. Ahead lie the Sir Francis Drake Channel, Anguilla, Basseterre and Antigua, with days at sea between.

Crags at breakfast, a private island by nightfall. Aboard National Geographic Resolution, this voyage links the Society Islands to the Tuamotus. Bora Bora brings the peaks of Mount Otemanu into view one morning, then an evening barbecue with music on a private motu. Taha'a makes you choose: snorkel where blacktip reef sharks may appear, or go ashore to a family-run vanilla farm. Fakarava gets two days to itself. Tip: fly into Papeete with time to spare, since check-in at the hospitality desk happens that afternoon, before you board.

/journeys/cruise/ponant-explorations-arc.note: Ice and Inuit culture, the title promises, and the route obliges. Le Commandant Charcot leaves Nuuk and gives you a full day at sea to find your footing before the real business begins. Disko Bay is the heart of it, held across Days 3–4 rather than rushed. Qeqertarsuaq follows, then Baffin Bay on the Canadian side, then Sisimiut, also lingered over. The loop closes back at Nuuk. Arctic Spring, 8 days. A practical thought: spend Day 2 unpacking, reading up and learning the ship, so Disko Bay gets your full attention.

/journeys/cruise/ponant-explorations-in-.note: 19 days aboard L'Austral, tracing the Northwest Passage from Greenland into Canada's Arctic islands and back. It opens in Kangerlussuaq, above the Arctic Circle, where the tundra turns autumnal and musk oxen, reindeer and Arctic foxes go about their business. Then the ice country: Bellot Strait, Beechey Island, and Devon Island not once but twice. The tip: Kangerlussuaq's international airport is your way in, and the Greenland ice sheet sits within reach of town. Arrive with time to get close to it before sailing. The journey finishes in Nuuk.

/journeys/cruise/ponant-explorations-nat.note: Le Soléal sails from Manila to Keelung, from the Philippines to Taiwan, on a route that promises nature and heritage in the same breath. The names do half the selling. Corregidor Island. Hundred Islands. Batanes, the final Philippine call before Kaohsiung. The whole affair runs 9 days under the PONANT EXPLORATIONS flag. A practical thought: plan around the day at sea near the end, the one stretch with no port listed. Save the packing for it, and let the last leg to Keelung pass unhurried.

/journeys/cruise/quark-expeditions-canad.note: It starts gently, in Reykjavík, with a hotel covered by the Charter Flight & Hotel Package and a free day among the city's modern architecture and Viking history. Get in on Day 1 and spend it properly. Then a charter flight to Nuuk, Greenland's capital, and aboard Ultramarine. A sea day over the Davis Strait brings polar presentations from the Expedition Team. After that, the Northwest Passage itself: Pond Inlet, Beechey Island, and one day simply marked Captain's Choice. Wildlife and helicopters, the billing promises. 19 days, flying out from Kangerlussuaq.

/journeys/cruise/seabourn-arctic-northwe.note: A long sweep from top to bottom of the map. Seabourn Venture spends its early weeks threading the Northwest Passage and lingering off Ellesmere Island, then turns south past the fjords of Labrador, through the Lesser Antilles, over the Equator and on to Rio De Janeiro. 71 days in all, with generous sea days to absorb it. The practical part comes first. The journey opens in Reykjavík, then takes to the air for Kangerlussuaq, so arrive in Reykjavík rested, with time in hand before that flight.

/journeys/cruise/seabourn-labrador-coast.note: Seabourn Venture, 39 days, and a route that refuses to settle. It begins in Reykjavík, flies you to Kangerlussuaq, then works along the Labrador coast by way of Nachvak Fjord and the Eclipse Channel. Later comes Devil's Island in French Guiana, a crossing of the Equator, and a long run down the Brazilian coast to Parati and Rio de Janeiro. Generous stretches at sea between. Practical note: the opening days are in Reykjavík, with air travel on Day 2, so arrive in Iceland with time in hand.

/journeys/cruise/seabourn-ultimate-green.note: Fjords, straits and a very long horizon. Seabourn Venture leaves Reykjavík and threads its way through Greenland, Nunavut and the Labrador coast over 79 days, finally tying up in Halifax. The character is in the crossings: the Northwest Passage comes back again and again, and Ellesmere Island gets several days to itself. Nuuk and Kangerlussuaq come round more than once, so there is no need to cram them on the first pass. Plenty of days at sea, too. Pack a stack of books and treat them as rest days, not gaps.

/journeys/cruise/seabourn-wild-british-i.note: Seabourn Venture leaves Greenwich and reaches Reykjavík the long way: 26 days, island by island. Small names, mostly. Lundy. Bardsey. Rathlin. Fair Isle and Mousa on a single day. The Faroe Islands claim their own stretch, from Vágur through Tórshavn to Oyndarfjørður, before Iceland closes things out with Grimsey and Dynjandi. A full route. Plan around the sea days, one after Belfast and another after Lerwick and Noss. They are the natural place to rest, read and let the next landfall come to you.

/journeys/cruise/swan-hellenic-new-zeala.note: Swan Hellenic's SH Minerva gives New Zealand 13 days, setting out from Dunedin and finishing in Auckland. The heart of it is the sounds. Dusky, Doubtful, then Milford, one after the other. Later comes Abel Tasman National Park, and a late call in the Bay of Islands. Plan around Day 3, when the ship takes in two sounds in a single day. Keep the camera charged and stay near the rail. A day at sea follows Wellington, a quiet pause before Tauranga. Book it through Aspen Travel Advisors.

/journeys/jet/abercrombie-and-kent-argen.note: 12 days, and the map does the heavy lifting. You begin in Buenos Aires. Day 4 brings Patagonia, Day 6 Puerto Natales, Day 7 Mendoza. Iguassu Falls waits for Day 10, and Sao Paulo has the final word on Day 12. Between them, a private jet and three countries in the title. There is no fixed calendar to bend to. The journey runs on request, so choose the start date that suits you and ask Aspen to shape the rest around it.

/journeys/jet/national-geographic-around.note: Around the world by private jet, 25 days, operated by National Geographic. Washington, D.C. at both ends. In between, Easter Island, a crossing of the International Date Line, then Petra and Marrakech before the last leg home. The route forks more than once: Machu Picchu or Trujillo, the Great Barrier Reef or the Daintree Rainforest, the Serengeti Plains or Ngorongoro Crater. Each pick shapes several days of the journey. So settle your choices well before you pack, and pack for the ones you chose.

/journeys/jet/remote-lands-china-s-unesc.note: China by private jet. Over a 12-night run the route moves from Beijing to Hangzhou, Lijiang and Shanghai, taking in five UNESCO World Heritage Sites, the Great Wall and Zhangjiajie's misty peaks among them. Beds come courtesy of three Aman properties. Aboard the jet every drink is included, alcohol too, so the hops between cities feel more lounge than transfer. A practical note: private car, driver and guide typically run 09:00 – 17:00, so keep evenings loose for your own wandering once the guide clocks off.

/journeys/jet/tcs-world-travel-exploring.note: Africa, taken from above and then on foot. The customised private jet does the hard yards, lifting off from Barcelona and setting down in Madrid. In between: the Nile, Ngorongoro Crater, Victoria Falls, Volcanoes National Park. Safari game drives. A trek to see mountain gorillas where they live. The world's largest caldera, and its largest waterfall too. Drinks flow aboard the jet, transfers are private, and a physician travels with the expedition team. Practical point: the journey ends in Madrid, not where it began, so book your flight home from there.

/journeys/jet/tcs-world-travel-wildlife-.note: Five landscapes, one private aircraft, and nobody fumbling for tip money. The trip opens at Big Sky, where Montana's rivers are there to be rafted, then moves on to Arenal Volcano National Park and volcanic trails under Costa Rica's green canopy. Later come the mirror-still waterways of the Amazon, and snorkel time off the Galápagos and in the Sea of Cortez. Hotels, meals, drinks aboard the jet, guides and every tip are folded in. Worth acting on: add the Banff start, and let the Canadian Rockies warm you up before the main event.

/journeys/safari/abercrombie-and-kent-a-.note: A Tanzania safari over 9 days, and none of them borrowed from someone else's calendar. It runs on request, so the dates bend to you rather than the other way round. You set out from Arusha and head into Tarangire National Park, then the heart of it: Ngorongoro, followed by the Serengeti, names that do most of the talking on their own. Abercrombie & Kent runs the ground; the booking sits with Aspen. The practical move is to settle your travel window first, then have Aspen build the departure around it.

/journeys/safari/abercrombie-and-kent-co.note: Quito first, then the islands. The route strings together Espanola, Floreana, Santa Cruz, Bartolome and South Plaza, one coastal landscape after another, all in the Galápagos of Ecuador. It is a private journey, so the travelling party is yours alone. No fixed calendar, either. The trip is arranged on request, with dates shaped to you inside the stated departure window. The practical move: settle on your preferred dates early, then have Aspen Travel Advisors build the trip around them, beginning in Quito. Islands on your schedule. Hard to argue with.

/journeys/safari/abercrombie-and-kent-ha.note: Hawai'i, one island at a time. Oahu opens with historic Pearl Harbor. Lanai swaps it for trails scented with pine. Then Maui: volcanic summits, and the storied Road to Hana, with Hana itself on Day 11, so keep something in reserve for it. Over 12 days the guiding is private, and any special equipment the activities need is supplied. There is no fixed calendar. The trip runs on request, so choose dates that suit you, not a timetable. A final document package lands before you leave.

/journeys/safari/african-travel-discover.note: Baobabs first, with elephants ambling between them in Tarangire. Then the Ngorongoro Crater, where predator and prey share the ground. Then the Serengeti, plains without end, the bush keeping its rhythm around the clock. It is a luxury flying safari through Northern Tanzania, with exceptional camps and lodges along the way. The practical bit: departures are on request, not fixed, so build the dates around yourself, and leave room for the balloon safari over the Serengeti, vistas and all.

/journeys/safari/andbeyond-bushman-natur.note: Open plains, and a walk at the pace of the people who know them. Camp staff drawn from local San Bushmen clans lead these interpretive walks near camp, sharing a traditional lifestyle through dress and activity. You follow paths where animals roam freely. Slow, deliberately so. Humbling, too. The journey runs 4 days in Botswana's Kalahari Desert, with andBeyond as operator. No fixed calendar: it runs on request, so choose your dates and let Aspen build the trip around them. Ask Aspen what the fare covers before you commit.

/journeys/safari/andbeyond-hot-air-ballo.note: Dawn over the Serengeti, and the only plan is the wind. The balloon drifts wherever the morning air decides, while the pilot works the altitude: down at treetop height for close looks at the wildlife below, then high enough to take in the full panorama. Now and then the burners whisper. In between, you simply drift. There is no fixed calendar; the safari runs on request, so dates are shaped around you. Tip: keep the camera ready on the low passes, when the best photographs come.

/journeys/safari/artisans-of-leisure-fam.note: Quito first. Then the Galápagos Islands from Day 3, and Guayaquil to close, all inside 8 days. The islands stay is land-based. Everything is private and pitched at families, with cultural touring in the two cities. Guides and drivers are yours alone. Internal transport, flights included, plus airport transfers and admission fees, is folded in. Support runs around the clock. No fixed calendar here. Departures run on request, so choose dates that suit the family. Then put the included restaurant and spa reservations to work early.

/journeys/safari/wilderness-desert-explo.note: Namibia, the dramatic version. Tall dunes at Sossusvlei, the far reaches of the Skeleton Coast, and Damaraland, where elephants have adapted to the desert and you might just meet one. Wilderness camps keep things comfortable. Days bring quad bikes, desert drives and coastal excursions, with safari activities twice a day. Meals, park fees and transfers are covered, and so is laundry, so pack light. The tip: on the private reserve near Sossusvlei, say yes to a night sleeping out on the roof. Dates are shaped around you.

/journeys/train/adams-and-butler-8-days-.note: Steam, and tickets for the Jacobite. This is Scotland by rail and road, starting in Glasgow and swinging north to Fort William. A driver guide handles 5 days, so you watch the window, not the map. Then Inverness, then Edinburgh to finish, with a walking tour in Glasgow and another in Edinburgh. Private transfers take care of the airport runs. There is no fixed calendar. The journey runs on request, so the dates are yours. Tip: Glasgow comes first, so arrive with energy for its walking tour.

/journeys/train/belmond-trains-taste-of-.note: Three days, two nights, and the Highlands arrive at the window. The Royal Scotsman leaves from Edinburgh and calls at Dundee, a steward on hand around the clock. Days bring a barbecue lunch at Rothiemurchus Estate, with lessons in survival skills from Ghillie Basan and Zeki, her son, then a turn at the Strathisla Distillery. Evenings: ceilidhs and the Observation Car. Every drink is included, the strong stuff too. One tip: rail constraints make timings indicative, so plan onward connections around your final itinerary, not the estimate.

/journeys/train/keytours-vacations-switz.note: Snow on the peaks, light on the lakes, and the view doing most of the work. You start in Zurich, then ride the rails to St. Moritz, glamorous in the Engadin Valley. The Glacier Express carries you over mountain passes to Zermatt and the Matterhorn. Interlaken opens onto the Jungfrau Region, and Lucerne brings it to a close, with a private transfer to Zurich Airport. 11 days, no fixed calendar. Tip: since departures are built on request, choose your dates first, then pick the hotels and activities to suit.

/journeys/train/la-dolce-vita-orient-exp.note: Rome at one end, Palermo at the other, and between them a train with no need to hurry. Naples arrives on the first day, and Taormina has the second all to itself. At the table, the cooking is Michelin 3-star, poured alongside Italian wines of the finest sort. The fare covers a transfer to and from the railway station, so leave the taxi rank to others and arrive unflustered. No fixed timetable here. It runs on request, and you choose the dates.

Rome Ostiense, morning, and the train pulls away. Lunch is the work of Heinz Beck, Michelin-starred and cooking with what the season brings. By afternoon you are in Montalcino, free to wander its streets. Ask ahead for the optional winery visit: Brunello in the glass, Tuscan food on the plate, and it only happens on request. Back aboard, dinner turns elegant, then live music, then sleep to the sway of the rails. The fare covers Italian wines at table and transfers to and from the station. Departures are arranged around you.

/journeys/worldcruise/regent-seven-seas-.note: One ship, Seven Seas Splendor, and 128 days from Miami to Civitavecchia. Two canals bookend the voyage: Panama early on, Suez near the close. Between them, the map fills with names that rarely share a sentence. Moorea and Huahine. Sydney and Cairns. Komodo, Phuket, Muscat, Rhodes. The tip: Bora Bora is called at twice, either side of Papeete, so there is no need to cram it all into the first visit. Save something for the second. Then let the long middle stretch do its work.

/journeys/worldcruise/seabourn-grand-exp.note: A voyage that starts in Reykjavík and finishes in Ushuaia, with the long way round in between: 95 days aboard Seabourn Venture. The character comes early, in repeated passes through the Northwest Passage and calls among the fjords of Greenland and Labrador, Nachvak and Saglek among them. Then the mood turns, through Caribbean bays and down the Brazilian coast to Rio De Janeiro. Pace yourself. South Georgia comes late, across Days 83–85, and deserves fresh legs.

/journeys/yacht/aman-at-sea-capri-and-am.note: Six days, one ship, and a run of Italian names that does most of the talking. Amangati, operated by Aman at Sea, sets out from Salerno and finishes in Naples. In between, two calls give the trip its shape: Amalfi on the second day, then Capri on the third. Sorrento and Ischia follow, unhurried. The practical bit: the voyage ends in Naples rather than where it began, so plan your onward travel from there, not from Salerno.

/journeys/yacht/four-seasons-yachts-gran.note: Las Palmas to the Caribbean in 12 days, aboard Four Seasons I. An Atlantic crossing, plainly put. You leave from Las Palmas, call at Santa Cruz De La Palma, and then the route goes quiet: nothing is listed between Day 2 and Day 9. Plan for that long stretch aboard, and bring the books to match. Then the islands come in a rush, Gustavia on Saint Barthélemy the one the voyage names in its title, before it ends at St. John's, Antigua.

/journeys/yacht/orient-express-sailing-y.note: A short voyage with a change of country in the middle. The Orient Express Olympian sails from Italy into France, and the trip's character sits right there at its heart. Portofino first. Then Cannes the following day, and Italy gives way to France. It is a one-way passage: you board in Naples and step off in Marseille. So book your journey home out of Marseille, not Naples. Reach Naples before day one rather than racing to meet it.

Sketches of Andalusia, drawn from the deck of the Orient Express Corinthian. The route opens in Málaga and calls at Gibraltar before it slows down. Motril is where it lingers, holding the yacht across Days 3–4, the one stretch with room to breathe. Use it. Keep one of those days loose rather than filling both, and let the pace drop. Majorca closes the voyage. Short, unhurried, and under sail, which is rather the point of a sailing yacht.

The Leeward Isles in 8 days, under sail aboard the Orient Express Corinthian, island to island across the Caribbean. You join at Marigot on Saint Martin and leave at Bridgetown, Barbados, so book flights in to one and home from the other. Gustavia, on Saint Barthélemy, sets the tone early. Then the pause. The route stays at Falmouth, Antigua, across Days 5–6. Two days, one port. Leave them loose and let the island set the pace. Booked through Aspen Travel Advisors.

/journeys/yacht/ritz-carlton-yacht-colle.note: Ilma, of the Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, slips out of Piraeus and into the Aegean. The Greek calls come quickly. Mílos early, its name doing half the work. Pátmos midway, softer and quieter on the tongue. Then the yacht points toward Türkiye, and the ending is the point. Istanbul claims the final stretch of the route, Days 7–8, not a hurried last morning. So plan for it. Keep those days loose, book nothing rigid, and give the city the time the itinerary gives it.

Evrima, the Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection ship, casts off from Tilbury in the United Kingdom and finishes in Bordeaux. In between comes a run of French calls: Honfleur early, La Rochelle later. Saint Peter Port, Guernsey, is the one stop along the way not filed under France. The ending is the point. Bordeaux holds Days 7–8, two days on the route rather than a hurried farewell. Plan around it. Keep onward travel clear until the second Bordeaux day is done, and let the city have both. Arrange it all through Aspen Travel Advisors.
